samples.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently turns the loss path from "archive the work" into "delete the work" — the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" is wrong
samples.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` and only `console.warn`s. But that handler is the *only* caller of `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())`, and `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771, 791: `const losing = this.expectedLosses.has(documentKey)` / `if (record && losing)`) archives **only** when the latch is set; otherwise it deletes the snapshot, header and change log outright (lines 809-811). The SDK calls `remove()` on the three paths where local work could not be reconciled, so if the pinned SDK (`@yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22`, per packages/frontend/package.json:99) rejects that event name — the exact scenario the new try/catch was added for — unsent edits are destroyed instead of archived, nothing is ever offered back by `offerRecoverableWork`, and because `reportLoss()` also never fires, `durable` stays true so the chip keeps reading "Saved to this device". That is simultaneously data loss and the over-report the feature says it must never make, with no signal beyond a console warning. If the event is genuinely unsupported the safe behaviour is to degrade the durability claim (e.g. latch `writesFailing`/`persistDisabled`) rather than proceed as if durability held.

samples.summary: The new `continue` treats every non-404 failure as "leave archived", but archives are unconditionally swept at 30 days, so a persistently failing `fetchDocument` loses the work without ever offering it
samples.evidence: `if (!(err instanceof HttpError) || err.status !== 404) { ...; continue; }` relies on the stated contract that "an archive left in place is offered again next session, so an unclear answer costs a delay and nothing more". That is not true indefinitely: `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale()` drops archives by `archivedAt` on the same 30-day cutoff as live entries (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1190, `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)`), and it runs first on every mount of this component (offline-runtime.tsx:111). A user whose session is repeatedly offline/5xx for a month never gets the offer and the archive is then deleted. Also note `fetchDocument` can throw a plain `Error('Document not found')` on a 200 with an empty body (api/documents.ts:52-54), which this branch treats as "unclear" even though it means the document is gone.

samples.summary: The caught error is not included in the warning, making the non-404 skip undiagnosable
samples.evidence: `console.warn('[offline] leaving work archived: could not confirm the document is gone')` drops `err`, unlike every other warn in this file (e.g. line 151 `console.warn('[offline] could not reconcile local copies:', err)`). When recovery silently declines for a whole population of users there is no status code or message in the log to tell 403 from a network failure.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:268-285 swallows a throwing doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...) with only a console.warn, and that handler (line 282-283) is the sole production caller of store.expectLoss and reportLoss (grep shows all other expectLoss callers are tests). Without the latch, wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771/791 evaluates `losing` false and lines 809-811 delete snapshot, header and change log with no archive written, so offerRecoverableWork (offline-runtime.tsx:180,212) can never hand the work back; simultaneously `durable` (line 181) stays true and `lapse` (199-207) stays undefined, so the chip keeps claiming local durability. I could not refute on reachability: supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82; collab-document-provider.tsx:223) gates the durable client on the @yorkie-js/react pin reaching 0.7.23, but it is a version gate on the clientKey prop, not a guard on event support, and no code anywhere converts a failed subscription into writesFailing/persistDisabled. The SDK is not vendored (no node_modules), so I cannot establish that the event name is accepted — the file's own comment at 262-265 asserts it may not be. Swallowed error handling leading to deletion of unreconciled local work is squarely in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: `DurableLossWatch` calls `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped'/'persist-disabled')` with no try/catch; an unsupported event name throws out of a passive effect and unmounts the whole editor subtree
finding.evidence: The effect guards only for `typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function'`, then calls `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` and `doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', ...)` unguarded. Yorkie's `Document.subscribe` rejects unknown event names (it throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` for a first string argument that is neither a known keyword nor a `$`-path). The repo pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.22 while `supportsClientKey()` gates only on the `@yorkie-js/react` pin (`__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, yorkie-capabilities.ts:74-81) — so bumping react to 0.7.23 without the sdk activates this path against an sdk that may not know `persist-disabled`. The sibling component in this very change documents the consequence and defends against it: "a throw from a passive effect unmounts the tree: a missing avatar is a blemish, a blank editor is an outage" (collab-document-provider.tsx:83-85), and wraps its work in try/catch. This one does not. Secondary: if the second `subscribe` throws after the first succeeded, no cleanup is returned and the first subscription leaks.

verdict.reason: The finding claims DurableLossWatch calls both doc.subscribe(...) calls "unguarded" with "no try/catch". The working tree contradicts this. durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:269-278 defines a watch(subscribe) helper whose body is: try { const unsubscribe = subscribe(); if (typeof unsubscribe === 'function') unsubscribers.push(unsubscribe); } catch (err) { console.warn('[offline] could not watch a durability event:', err); }. Both subscriptions go through it: lines 280-284 wrap doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...) and lines 292-296 wrap doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', ...). Lines 263-267 explicitly document the exact hazard the reviewer raises (YorkieError ErrInvalidArgument 'Unsupported event type' thrown from a passive effect unmounting the subtree) as the reason the guard exists, so an unknown-event throw on an older SDK is caught and downgraded to a console.warn; the editor subtree is not unmounted. The secondary leak claim is likewise not present: each successful unsubscribe is pushed into unsubscribers (line 273) before the next watch call runs, and because watch swallows the throw the effect still reaches its unconditional cleanup return (lines 297-307), which iterates unsubscribers and calls each unsubscribe inside its own try/catch. The comparison to the sibling component is also inaccurate: PresenceIdentityRepair (collab-document-provider.tsx:86-120) uses a capability check plus try/catch, and DurableLossWatch uses a capability check (line 258) plus per-subscription try/catch - the same defense at finer granularity. The version-pin premise (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82 gating only on __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__) is factually correct but only establishes reachability of a throw that the existing catch already absorbs.
